nodes.content: Develop image classifiers whose adversarial robustness generalizes to unseen corruption distributions while preserving clean accuracy.
requirements: At ℓ∞ ε=8/255, exceed matched adversarial training’s worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C robust accuracy by ≥5 percentage points.
Keep clean CIFAR-10 accuracy within 1 percentage point of baseline, without corruption-specific training or adaptation.

nodes.content: Augment ε=8/255 adversarial training with wavelet-band Jacobian penalties and clean-teacher distillation, using only uncorrupted CIFAR-10 training images.
Can wavelet-band Jacobian penalties improve worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C adversarial accuracy while clean-teacher distillation prevents clean-accuracy loss?
Wavelet penalties plus distillation raise worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C PGD-20 accuracy ≥5 points versus matched adversarial training, with ≤1-point clean-accuracy loss.
Train matched PGD-AT and wavelet-penalty/distillation models on clean CIFAR-10; compare ε=8/255 PGD-20 worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C and clean accuracy.
Train three-seed WideResNet-28-10 PGD-AT controls and wavelet-penalty/distillation variants on clean CIFAR-10 with identical ε=8/255 schedules.
Six WideResNet-28-10 checkpoints and training logs: three matched PGD-AT controls and three wavelet-penalty/distillation models.
Score six checkpoints across 75 CIFAR-10-C corruption-severities using ε=8/255 PGD-20; compare worst-corruption robustness and clean CIFAR-10 accuracy.
Three-seed worst-corruption PGD-20 accuracy rose from 7.8% to 10.9%, missing the five-point target; clean accuracy fell 0.4 points.
Clean-data sensitivity-weighted wavelet penalties should deliver ≥5-point worst-corruption PGD-20 gains versus PGD-AT, with distillation keeping ≤1-point clean loss.
Fine-tune n7’s three wavelet checkpoints with clean-image sensitivity-weighted penalties; benchmark against n7 controls on PGD-20 CIFAR-10-C and clean accuracy.
Three-seed worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C PGD-20 accuracy reached 13.4% versus 7.8% controls (+5.6 points); clean accuracy fell 0.7 points.
Advance sensitivity-weighted penalties to AutoAttack validation: PGD-20 clears both targets, but single-attack results cannot establish robust accuracy.
Train three-seed wavelet-only and distillation-only ablations; compare with n7 checkpoints on CIFAR-10-C PGD-20 robustness and clean accuracy.
Worst-corruption PGD-20 accuracy and clean-accuracy change: wavelet-only 10.0%, −1.3 points; distillation-only 8.1%, −0.1; combined 10.9%, −0.4.
Distill complementary decision boundaries from n7’s PGD-AT and wavelet checkpoints into one student via clean-image adversarial disagreement mining.
Mine n7 teacher disagreements on clean CIFAR-10, distill three students, compare worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C ε=8/255 AutoAttack and clean accuracy against PGD-AT.
Mine n7 clean-image teacher disagreements; distill three students; benchmark against n7 wavelet/PGD-AT checkpoints on ε=8/255 CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack and clean accuracy.
Three-seed worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack accuracy: students 5.9% versus n7 PGD-AT 6.1%; clean accuracy fell 0.3 points.
Does clean-image disagreement mining concentrate on brittle high-frequency features, explaining students’ lower AutoAttack robustness than PGD-AT?
High-frequency teacher disagreements cause students’ 5.9% AutoAttack accuracy; filtering the highest wavelet-energy quartile should exceed PGD-AT’s 6.1%.
Stratify teacher disagreements by high-frequency wavelet energy; retrain three students excluding the top quartile and compare worst-corruption AutoAttack accuracy.
High-frequency top-quartile disagreements accounted for 42% of student errors; filtering raised worst-corruption AutoAttack accuracy from 5.9% to 7.0%.
Defer disagreement distillation: filtering improves worst-corruption AutoAttack accuracy from 5.9% to 7.0%, still below PGD-AT’s 11.1% target.
Compare filtered-student and PGD-AT AutoAttack failures across CIFAR-10-C corruption types to document why deferred distillation misses target.
CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack failure atlas with per-corruption accuracy tables and overlapping-error counts for filtered students versus PGD-AT.
Train with worst-case clean-derived Fourier-band amplitude reweighting inside PGD, using teacher distillation to protect clean accuracy.
Can clean-derived Fourier-band reweighting improve worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack accuracy without distillation exceeding the clean-accuracy budget?
Audit n26’s failures; train three clean-only Fourier-PGD/distillation models, then measure ε=8/255 worst-corruption AutoAttack and clean accuracy.
Three-seed Fourier-PGD averaged 12.0% worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack accuracy versus PGD-AT’s 6.1%, with 0.8-point clean-accuracy loss.
Fourier-PGD’s ≥5-point worst-corruption AutoAttack advantage over PGD-AT persists across independent training runs, with ≤1-point clean-accuracy loss.
Train five fresh paired PGD-AT/Fourier-PGD seeds without corruptions; compare worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C ε=8/255 AutoAttack, clean accuracy, and confidence intervals.
Train five new paired Fourier-PGD/PGD-AT seeds; bootstrap worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack gains and clean-accuracy losses at ε=8/255.
Five fresh pairs yielded worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack accuracy of 10.2% versus PGD-AT’s 6.3% (+3.9 points); clean accuracy fell 0.7 points.
Retune Fourier-band weights using clean-only adversarial validation; rerun five paired seeds before CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack and clean CIFAR-10 evaluation.
Use n26’s failure atlas to preregister evaluation strata; retune Fourier weights on clean-only adversarial validation and train five paired seeds.
Fourier-PGD v2 bundle containing clean-selected band weights, five paired model checkpoints per method, and preregistered evaluation strata.
Score n37’s five paired seeds across all 75 CIFAR-10-C conditions with ε=8/255 AutoAttack; report worst-corruption and clean accuracies.
Five-seed worst-corruption AutoAttack: Fourier-PGD v2 11.6% versus PGD-AT 6.3%, clean loss 0.8 points; filtered students rescued 6% of Fourier errors.
Select Fourier-PGD v2; test filtered-student ensembling for its 6% error rescue, retaining it only if clean accuracy stays within budget.
Ensemble Fourier-PGD v2 with filtered-disagreement students using clean-trained, differentiable logit gating to exploit complementary robust errors.
Differentiable clean-trained gating raises worst-corruption ε=8/255 AutoAttack accuracy ≥1 point above Fourier-PGD v2 without exceeding 1-point clean loss.
Train five clean-only differentiable gates combining Fourier-PGD v2 and filtered students; compare white-box ε=8/255 AutoAttack and clean accuracy.
Five-gate mean worst-corruption AutoAttack accuracy was 11.9% versus Fourier-PGD v2’s 11.6%; clean loss reached 1.2 points.
Can clean-logit regularization recover the gate’s 0.2-point excess clean loss without erasing its 0.3-point AutoAttack gain?
Sweep clean-logit KL weights on clean CIFAR-10 validation; retrain five gates and remeasure worst-corruption AutoAttack and clean loss.
Select KL weight from {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} on clean validation; retrain five gates and run full CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack.
Gate-KL evaluation bundle: selected clean-only KL weight, five gated checkpoints, and per-corruption AutoAttack and clean-accuracy tables.
Recompute paired ε=8/255 worst-corruption AutoAttack gains and clean-accuracy losses from n48, checking n42’s ≥1-point and ≤1-point thresholds.
Five-seed Gate-KL worst-corruption AutoAttack reached 12.8% versus Fourier-PGD v2’s 11.6% (+1.2 points); clean accuracy fell 0.9 points.
Train a multi-resolution shared-backbone classifier with joint native/half-resolution PGD attacks and clean-logit consistency, without corruption examples.
Does joint native/half-resolution adversarial training outperform Gate-KL on unseen CIFAR-10-C while keeping clean accuracy within baseline minus one point?
Multi-resolution PGD raises worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack accuracy ≥1 point over Gate-KL’s 12.8%, with ≤1-point clean-accuracy loss.
Initialize from n37 Fourier-PGD checkpoints; train five native/half-resolution PGD models with clean-logit consistency; compare ε=8/255 AutoAttack/clean accuracy against n48.
Five-seed worst-corruption CIFAR-10-C AutoAttack accuracy reached 14.0% versus Gate-KL’s 12.8%; clean accuracy fell 0.9 points versus baseline.
Select multi-resolution PGD over Gate-KL: 14.0% versus 12.8% worst-corruption AutoAttack accuracy at equal 0.9-point clean loss.
Freeze selected multi-resolution and matched PGD-AT checkpoints; independently audit all 75 CIFAR-10-C conditions with AutoAttack, PGD-100, and clean accuracy.
Audit five frozen model pairs across 75 CIFAR-10-C conditions using white-box AutoAttack and PGD-100 through the full preprocessing pipeline.
Frozen audit bundle with five paired checkpoints, per-corruption AutoAttack/PGD-100 results, clean accuracies, attack configurations, and reproducible evaluation scripts.
Reevaluate n37’s Fourier-PGD v2 alongside n59’s multi-resolution and PGD-AT checkpoints under identical AutoAttack/PGD-100 and clean-accuracy protocols.
Identical-pipeline audit confirmed 14.0% worst-corruption AutoAttack accuracy for multi-resolution versus 11.6% Fourier-PGD and 6.3% PGD-AT; clean loss was 0.9 points.
Supersede n40’s Fourier-PGD v2 with multi-resolution PGD: 14.0% versus 11.6% AutoAttack, 0.9-point clean loss; drop wavelet-only (1.3-point loss).
